acts.title: The jobs people stay in
text: The average person now changes employer about twelve times in a working life, and the figure is often used to prove that loyalty is dead. It proves nothing of the kind. The average hides two completely different groups.

In some professions people stay. Judges, nurses and teachers change employer rarely: the median nurse has been in health care for eleven years and in the same hospital for six. The work is difficult to enter, and once you are in, moving means starting the difficult part again somewhere else.

In others they move constantly. In advertising, construction and technology, four years in one company is a long time, and people who stay longer are sometimes asked why. One recruiter told us she reads five years in a job as “either very committed or slightly stuck”, and that she cannot tell which from the CV.

The interesting group is the third one, which the average erases entirely: people who leave a profession completely. About one nurse in four has left health care within ten years of qualifying, and most of them do not come back.
Ask somebody how long they have done their job and you learn one number. Ask them how long they intend to keep doing it, and you learn considerably more.

write.q: Write about your working or studying life: 6 sentences. Use for twice, since twice, one Past Simple with a finished date, and one used to about something that is no longer true.
write.model: I’ve worked at the same company for four years and I’ve been in this particular team since last March. I started here in 2020, three weeks before the office closed, so I have never seen most of my colleagues in the same room. I used to work in an open-plan office with about sixty people, and I do not miss it. My sister has been a nurse since 2011 and has been in the same hospital for six of those years. I’ve wanted to change field for about a year now. I haven’t done anything about it yet.

speak.q: Answer out loud: How long have you worked or studied where you are? When did you start? How long have you lived in your city? What did you use to do that you don’t do now?
speak.model: I’ve worked here for four years. I started in 2020. I’ve lived in this city since I was nineteen. I used to work in construction — I don’t any more.
